original_value: Socio-ecological systems are recognized as complex adaptive systems whose multiple interactions might change as a response to external or internal changes. Due to its complexity, the behavior of the system is often uncertain. Bayesian networks provide a sound approach for handling complex domains endowed with uncertainty. The aim of this paper is to analyze the impact of the Bayesian network structure on the uncertainty of the model, expressed as the Shannon entropy. In particular, three strategies for model structure have been followed: naive Bayes (NB), tree augmented network (TAN) and network with unrestricted structure (GSS). Using these network structures, two experiments are carried out: (1) the impact of the Bayesian network structure on the entropy of the model is assessed and (2) the entropy of the posterior distribution of the class variable obtained from the different structures is compared. The results show that GSS constantly outperforms both NB and TAN when it comes to evaluating the uncertainty of the entire model. On the other hand, NB and TAN yielded lower entropy values of the posterior distribution of the class variable, which makes them preferable when the goal is to carry out predictions.

result.paraphrase: Socio-ecological systems are regarded as complex adaptive systems in which many interactions can shift in response to external or internal changes. Because of this complexity, system behavior is often uncertain. Bayesian networks offer a robust way to manage complex domains characterized by uncertainty. This paper examines how Bayesian network structure affects model uncertainty, measured by Shannon entropy. Three structural strategies are considered: naive Bayes (NB), tree-augmented network (TAN), and unrestricted-structure network (GSS). With these structures, two experiments are performed: first, to assess the effect of network structure on the model’s entropy; second, to compare the entropy of the class variable’s posterior distribution across the different structures. The findings indicate that GSS consistently outperforms both NB and TAN in evaluating the uncertainty of the full model. By contrast, NB and TAN produce lower entropy values for the class variable’s posterior distribution, making them better suited for prediction tasks.
